originalTitle: Germany blames Russia for drone attack at Leipzig airport
summary: Government says ‘dangerous behaviour’ is part of effort by Moscow to cause damage with hybrid attacks
content: The German government has blamed Russia for the drone attack on Leipzig airport last month, calling it “dangerous behaviour” and part of a systematic and concerted effort by Moscow to “cause great damage” through a large number of hybrid attacks. The interior minister, Alexander Dobrindt, and the foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, ended weeks of speculation and the government’s hesitancy to blame Russia, saying in a brisk 10-minute briefing in Berlin that all indications were the Russian state had provided the knowhow and equipment for the planned attack and “low-level agents” were recruited to carry it out. A drone loaded with explosives was discovered at Leipzig/Halle airport on 4 August attached to the wing of a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane used to transport weapons to Ukraine. It failed to detonate but could have caused a catastrophe, authorities said. Russia will face a package of penalty measures, Wadephul said, adding that the German government saw “a need for appropriate and necessary action in this situation”. It would respond “to this hybrid attack in Leipzig with proportionate and measured, yet equally resolute, action”, he said. “We are not at war, but we are a daily target of hybrid warfare.” He added: “The dangerous behaviour of the Russian Federation is part of attempts at destabilisation, disinformation, threats, sabotage and aggression.” Berlin regretted the abysmal state of its relations with Moscow, he said. The EU expressed “full solidarity” with Germany over the attack, and Nato assured Berlin that it would defend its members. Russian president Vladimir Putin called the sanctions “another mistake,” suggesting the restrictions were aimed at currying favour with voters. “I think it’s another mistake, a serious one,” Putin said during a press conference broadcast by the Russian state news agency Tass. “And in my view it clearly runs counter to the interests of the German people.” The Russian ambassador had been summoned to the foreign ministry at that very moment to be informed of the consequences, Wadephul said. The Russian consulate in Bonn will be closed later this month, and Russian House, a sprawling cultural and science institute in the centre of Berlin, which is alleged to house Russian spies and to have been the launchpad for a number of hybrid attacks carried out in Germany over the past few years, is to be turned out of its rented building. A clampdown on Russia’s shadow fleet – illegal ships carrying Russian oil and other supplies in the Baltic and North seas – is also planned. Sweden and Finland track and disrupt the shadow fleet but Germany does not, so vessels regularly opt to sail via German waters in its foreign economic zones. New lists of people on a blacklist would be drawn up and tighter border controls of Russians entering Germany would be carried out, Wadephul said. Parallel to these moves, Berlin is also backing the European Commission’s 22nd package of sanctions, to cover a further 1,600 companies and organisations with a Russian connection. The government has previously said it does not intend to directly involve Nato by invoking article 4 of the alliance. However, its Nato and European partners were informed about the investigation and agreed on the planned consequences, Wadephul confirmed. The Nato secretary general, Mark Rutte, and the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, promised “full solidarity” with Berlin. Rutte said Berlin had put forward clear evidence of Moscow’s role in the “hybrid attack” and welcomed the measures announced in response, while von der Leyen vowed to “keep the EU united despite these escalating and serious acts”. Tuesday’s announcement marks the first time the German government has concretely named Russia as responsible for the attack. It marks the lowest point in decades for relations between Russia and the EU’s largest member, which had already plunged after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. This weekend will see a critical election in the eastern states of Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg Vorpommern, in which the war in Ukraine and relations with Russia have been a focal point. The far-right populist Alternative für Deutschland, which is pushing a pro-Russia agenda as it seeks to win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt, has accused the government of double standards over its treatment of Russia. Urging the government to prove Russia’s involvement in the Leipzig incident earlier this week, it said the same rigour should be applied to investigations into the attack on the Nord Stream pipeline, for which Ukraine is alleged to have been responsible. The drone in the Leipzig incident was carrying 600g of explosives and was discovered in the security area of the airport close to Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes on the night of 4-5 August. The explosive device detonator appeared to have failed. A second drone was believed to have been part of the planned attack but investigators have since thrown doubt on that theory. Traces of the military explosive hexogen were found on the edge of the airport on 14 August along with a further drone, investigators confirmed. Had the devices exploded they could have caused a catastrophe, German officials said. The chancellor, Friedrich Merz, who last week said whoever was behind the attack “will pay”, did not attend the briefing to the press and public on Tuesday. Konstantin von Notz, the Green party’s security policy expert and commissioner for intelligence oversight, criticised the government before the announcement for what he described as its failure to stand up to Putin in the face of the growing hybrid threat from Russia. “The federal government must finally stop being hesitant, reticent and timid. Things must be called by their name, and decisive action must be taken,” he said in an interview with the RND network. chineseTitle: 德国指责俄罗斯对莱比锡机场的无人机袭击负责
chineseSummary: 政府称“危险行为”是莫斯科通过混合攻击造成破坏的努力的一部分
chineseContent: 德国政府指责俄罗斯上个月对莱比锡机场发动无人机袭击，称其为“危险行为”，是莫斯科系统性、协调一致的努力的一部分，旨在通过大量混合袭击“造成巨大损失”。内政部长亚历山大·多布林特 (Alexander Dobrindt) 和外交部长约翰·瓦德菲尔 (Johann Wadephul) 结束了数周的猜测和政府对指责俄罗斯的犹豫，他们在柏林举行的 10 分钟简报中表示，所有迹象都表明俄罗斯政府为计划中的袭击提供了技术和设备，并招募了“低级别特工”来实施袭击。 8 月 4 日，在莱比锡/哈雷机场发现了一架装载爆炸物的无人机，该无人机附着在一架用于向乌克兰运输武器的乌克兰安东诺夫货机的机翼上。当局表示，虽然它未能爆炸，但可能会造成灾难。瓦德菲尔表示，俄罗斯将面临一系列惩罚措施，并补充说，德国政府认为“在这种情况下需要采取适当和必要的行动”。他说，它将“以适度、谨慎但同样坚决的行动来应对莱比锡的这种混合袭击”。 “我们没有处于战争状态，但我们每天都是混合战争的目标。”他补充说：“俄罗斯联邦的危险行为是破坏稳定、虚假信息、威胁、破坏和侵略企图的一部分。”他说，柏林对其与莫斯科的糟糕关系感到遗憾。欧盟就袭击事件向德国表示“全力声援”，北约向柏林保证将保卫其成员国。俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京称制裁是“另一个错误”，并暗示这些限制旨在讨好选民。普京在新闻发布会上表示：“我认为这是另一个错误，而且是一个严重的错误。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
